Applying this choice to two projections in each of 32 layers gives $4\,194\,304$ trainable factor parameters if both projections are square. ### Compare target modules at the same parameter budget [Llama 3 8B](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.21783v3#S3.T3) also has 32 layers and a hidden width of 4,096, but it has 32 query heads and only eight K/V heads. Each head has width $4096/32=128$. A value projection therefore returns $8\cdot128=1024$ coordinates, while a query projection returns all 4,096. At rank 8, their LoRA branches have $8(4096+1024)=40\,960$ and $8(4096+4096)=65\,536$ parameters respectively. The model-wide total for query and value is $(65\,536+40\,960)\cdot32=3\,407\,872$. | Projections adapted in each block | Rank | Trainable factor parameters in 32 blocks | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Query and value | 8 | 3,407,872 | | All four attention projections | 4 | 3,407,872 | | All seven attention and FFN projections | 8 | 20,971,520 | The first two rows have the same budget: adding keys costs as much as adding values, and the attention output projection costs as much as queries. Halving the rank offsets doubling the sum of the projection dimensions. The third row includes three SwiGLU matrices that connect widths 4,096 and 14,336.
